_comment: Production configuration for FishMMO Discord Bot. Overrides Development defaults. The bot token MUST be set in the FISHMMO_DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable, and the database credentials in FISHMMO_DB_USERNAME / FISHMMO_DB_PASSWORD or /etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env (chmod 600). Do not commit real credentials here.

Discord._comment_token: There is no Token key: the bot reads its token only from the FISHMMO_DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable, and refuses to connect without it. Never commit the token to source control.
Discord._comment_guild_id: 0 means disabled. Set to a real Discord guild ID (snowflake) for the bot to operate in a specific server.

_comment_npgsql: Non-sensitive database settings, read by FishMMO-DB's NpgsqlDbConfiguration like every other FishMMO process; FISHMMO_DB_HOST / FISHMMO_DB_PORT / FISHMMO_DB_NAME override them. No credentials here (see _comment).
_comment_chat_relay: ChatRelay.GameToDiscordChannels is an ALLOWLIST of in-game chat channels the bot may republish to Discord. Omit it to use the built-in default (Say, World, Trade, Region) — public channels only. Tell, Guild and Party are private and are refused even if named here; making them relayable is a code change, not a config change.
_comment_bridge_length: BridgeMessageMaxLength caps a Discord message bridged into the game. Keep it at or below the game's ChatBroadcast.MaxTextLength (128) — clients discard anything longer, so a larger value makes long messages vanish rather than arrive truncated. This was 2000, so every bridged message over 128 characters was silently dropped by every client.
_comment_discord_verification: DiscordVerification delivers the Discord verification code: the game or Control Panel issues it, the bot DMs it, and the player types it back into the game or panel (never into Discord). The bot does not poll for codes: issuing one raises a PostgreSQL NOTIFY that the bot LISTENs for, a slow safety sweep every SweepMinutes (1-60) catches anything raised while the bot was down, and a player who has not joined the Discord server yet is sent the code from the member-joined event when they join. Each account gets exactly ONE DM, ever: there are no resends, and a send whose outcome Discord left unclear stays claimed for staff to check rather than risk a second DM. BatchSize is the most deliveries one pass reads; MinDmIntervalMs is the global minimum gap between any two DMs, so the bot cannot be used to spam. Discord:DefaultGuildId MUST be the server the game's invite link points players to: a bot can only find and DM members of a server it shares with them. 0 disables delivery.
